How to use Sebene

For anyone hosting a party from a Spotify playlist: let the agent run the evening on its own, or take over at any moment and start the right song at its hottest point.

Open Sebene ↗Platform detailsContact

Guided tourReal screens

Plays automatically. Use the dots or arrows to move, Pause to stop.

01

Getting started

1

Open sebene-party.vercel.app in Chrome on the computer connected to the speakers.

2

Sign in at open.spotify.com in the same browser. Without it Spotify plays only 30-second previews, and a red banner says so.

3

Press the big play button. Atalaku, the DJ agent, plays the hot part of each song and mixes it into the next.

4

Before the party, open The set, choose Needs a listen and press Soundcheck: each estimated cut plays for 12 seconds so you can confirm or move it.

5

Press Guide, at the top, for every control explained in plain words.

02

Features

01

Now playing

The record shows the whole song as its ring: the hot part glows on it and fills in as it plays, with the album cover spinning as the label. Under the title, the app says where the hot part sits, how it was found (Hook, Sebene or Estimate) and why, and counts down to the next mix.

STEPS

  1. Press play to start the set
  2. Tap the ring to jump to any moment
  3. Press Mix now to go to the next song
  4. Press Ride this song to let a favourite run past its hot part
02

Heaters and the crate

Every song, searchable and filtered by style. Heaters shows the eight hottest songs not played yet; one tap drops a song in right away, at its hot part. Each song in the crate also has Play now and Next.

STEPS

  1. Type a song or artist, or press the slash key
  2. Pick a style chip
  3. Tap a heater to drop it in now
  4. Tap Next to line a song up
03

Drag a song to Next

Grab any song by its dotted handle, in the crate or in the set, and drop it on the Next card or on Drop to play next, which appears at the bottom of the screen while you drag. Drop to play now mixes it in immediately. On a phone, drag from the handle so the list still scrolls.

STEPS

  1. Press and hold the dotted handle
  2. Drag to the Next card or the bar at the bottom
  3. Release on Drop to play next, or on Drop to play now
04

Your picks

Your picks always play before the agent's choices, in the order you set. The Next card shows the first pick and its hot part; the list under it numbers the others. Drag a pick to reorder it, or remove it with the cross.

STEPS

  1. Drag a pick up or down
  2. Tap the cross to remove one
  3. Tap clear to empty your picks
05

Never silent

The next song is loaded on the second player, already at its hot part, about 15 seconds early, and started just before the current cut ends. The current song stops only once the new one is sounding, then the two overlap for the blend time. If Spotify is still slow, a drum bridge keeps the beat, and a boom lands with the new song.

STEPS

  1. Choose Smooth blend, Quick blend or Hard cut in Mix settings
  2. Pick a transition sound and press Test
  3. Press Hear it to hear the drum bridge
06

Mix settings

Transition length, transition sound and its volume, the length of each cut (about 35, 55 or 85 seconds), the order (Thanksgiving arc, playlist order, peak-time energy or shuffle), the set length, the start time, the styles in the set and looping. Remix the order reshuffles the arc without breaking its rules.

STEPS

  1. Scroll to Mix settings
  2. Change a setting; the set and its timetable update at once
  3. Press Remix the order for a new running order
07

The set and Soundcheck

The set is a timetable: each cut with its start time, its hot part and how it was found, grouped by part of the evening. Needs a listen keeps only the estimated cuts, and Soundcheck plays each for 12 seconds. Start here saves the moment you hear as the new hot part; minus 5 s, plus 5 s, Shorter, Longer and Keep cut refine it, and the app remembers.

STEPS

  1. Choose Needs a listen
  2. Press Soundcheck
  3. Press Start here at the right moment, or Keep cut
08

Atalaku and new songs

Atalaku explains how it built the evening: songs read, repeats removed, how many hot parts came from lyric timing, when the dance floor starts and which song peaks it. Songs added to the Spotify playlist come in by pasted song links, or by connecting Spotify once so the playlist syncs every time Sebene opens.

STEPS

  1. In Spotify, open a song's menu, then Share, then Copy song link
  2. Paste the links in New songs and press Add songs
  3. Or connect Spotify with the Client ID of your own developer app
09

Party screen

A full-screen view for the TV: the spinning record, the song, its artist and what comes next, with play, Mix now, Hot part and Ride within reach. The screen stays awake while the music plays.

STEPS

  1. Press Party screen at the top
  2. Press Close or Escape to return
10

Guide

A guide inside the app covers preparation before the party, the controls during it, how transitions avoid silence, keyboard shortcuts and what to do if something goes wrong.

STEPS

  1. Press Guide at the top
  2. Press Close guide to return to the music
03Tips
  • Run the whole party from one computer signed in to Spotify. Cut corrections and added songs are kept in that browser; Copy my fixes and Paste fixes move them to another computer.
  • Leave Auto DJ on and use the heaters when the floor needs a lift; turn it off when you want every change to be yours.
  • Keyboard: Space plays or pauses, the right arrow mixes, H jumps to the hot part, M saves the moment as the hot part, R rides the song and the slash key searches.
04FAQ
How does it know the best part?

For 78 songs, synced lyrics from LRCLIB give the time of every line. The most repeated block of lines is the refrain, and in rumba and soukous the switch from long verses to short repeated shouts marks the sebene. The other songs are placed from how their style is usually built and marked Needs a listen.

Is there really no silence between songs?

No gap was measured, either on the live site with real Spotify players or under simulated slow and one-stream conditions. Spotify's players expose no volume control, so a blend is a short overlap rather than a fade.

Does it need Spotify Premium?

Full songs need the browser to be signed in to Spotify. Automatic playlist sync needs a Spotify developer app, which Spotify reserves for Premium accounts; adding songs by pasted links works without it.

Does it store lyrics?

No. Only the timing of the lines is used to place the cut. No lyric text is kept or shown.

Can it play another playlist?

It is built around one Thanksgiving playlist, and new songs join it by link or by sync. Another playlist would need its own crate of style and energy tags.

Why the name?

The sebene is the guitar-led dance section of Congolese rumba, where the floor fills; the atalaku is the animator who shouts over it. The app plays the sebene of every song, and its agent is called Atalaku.
